s: August 8, 2023 - The talus is the second largest bone in the hindfoot region of the human body. Responsible for transmitting body weight and forces passing between the lower leg and the foot[1] the talus is a component of many multiple joints, including the talocrural (ankle), subtalar, and transverse tarsal joints.[2] While the talus does not have any direct muscular attachments and has a tenuous and limited blood supply, it serves as the site of attachment for many ligaments including the lateral ankle ligaments and medial deltoid ligament complex.
